messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH priority alert — KV cache memory spike on prod-cluster-7, continuous-batching queue length > 10k, NCCL error bursts on TP group 4. Error rate (5m) up 6.2% — possible customer-facing latency/errors. Autodetect policy triggered.

oncall-lee: got the page, looking. any customer reports?

sre-maya: seeing sustained cache growth starting 23:04 UTC, correlates with rollout of lighter-batch policy 2026-03-15T23:00 (batch-config v2). KV shard distribution shows two shards at 78% mem and the rest <10%. NCCL logs show repeated handshake timeouts.

eng-runtime-jess: that skew looks like TP partitioning garbage collection isn't evicting prefixes. can we pause continuous batching?

oncall-lee: pausing batching on prod-cluster-7 now — running command: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/redwood/prod/clusters/7/actions/pause_continuous_batching`

incident-bot: Action accepted — continuous batching pause requested by oncall-lee.

eng-ml-aaron: fyi, model infra pushed quantized-kv hotpath yesterday; the new kernel may have different allocation patterns. if batching paused, we should still mitigate NCCL stalls by rebalancing shards.

infra-eli: starting soft-restart of TP group 4 nodes (rolling) to clear NCCL state. `kubectl rollout restart ds/tp-shard-4 -n prod` — doing one at a time.

cs-omar: we have inbound chat with two customers seeing large latency spikes (30-60s) and 503s. they're in EU region on dedicated. I flagged support ticket #INC-4103.

pm-anna: prioritizing impact comms. once we have ETA for full mitigation, push to affected customers.

eng-runtime-jess: quick hotfix suggestion: revert batching config to v1 defaults (max_batch_tokens=1024, prefix_cache_limit=2GB) — that should limit runaway cache growth. I can patch config and push canary to 10% traffic.

oncall-lee: do it. prefer canary first.

eng-runtime-jess: applying override: ```
PATCH /config/service/continuous_batching
{ "max_batch_tokens": 1024, "kv_prefix_cache_limit_bytes": 2147483648, "aggressive_prefetch": false }
```

incident-bot: Config override accepted, canary rollout 10% on prod-cluster-7 commencing.

eng-ml-aaron: checking KV shard map — looks like hashing function produced skew because of a new micro-shard mapping change last week. That plus larger per-batch prefix retention caused shard 2 to grow and start paging. paging -> increased host GPU memory pressure -> NCCL timeouts.

infra-eli: can confirm — GPU memory OOMs on gpuhost-27 leading to rpc retries. rolling restart helped clear some state, but unless we trim cache the issue will return.

eng-runtime-jess: evicting prefixes for shard 2 now: `./kvctl evict --cluster prod-cluster-7 --shard 2 --policy lru --percent 60`

oncall-lee: evict command issued. monitoring memory after evict.

incident-bot: Eviction job started; estimated 2-4 mins.

sre-maya: after eviction memory dropped ~45% on gpuhost-27, NCCL errors dropped sharply. front-end error rate trending back down to baseline.

cs-omar: told the affected customers we're mitigating; they asked for root cause and ETA. suggested message: "we identified a regression in continuous batching + KV shard mapping causing memory blowups; mitigation in progress, rolling fixes applied; customers on Dedicated may see intermittent latency, working on full fix" — ok to send?

pm-anna: ok to send brief update. follow-up note to include timeline and next steps once we rebalance.

eng-ml-aaron: next step is to compute new shard weights and schedule a controlled rebalance. I'll prepare a repro and patch to hashing code so new micro-shard mapping doesn't bias certain prefixes.

eng-runtime-jess: also recommend adding a safety limiter: `kv_prefix_cache_limit_bytes` per-shard enforced at runtime to avoid single shard blowups until hashing is fixed.

infra-eli: adding limiter now as cluster-level override: `kubectl apply -f kv-cache-limiter.yaml` — applied to prod-cluster-7; limiter set to 2.5GB per shard.

incident-bot: Cluster override applied.

oncall-lee: current status: continuous batching paused, canary reverted batching config to v1, eviction done, TP group rolling restart in progress, per-shard limiter applied. error rate back to near baseline, but we still see minor flaps on heavy prompts.

eng-ml-aaron: tagging this as regression caused by combo of (a) new batching defaults, (b) micro-shard mapping change, (c) quantized-kernel allocation change. plan: revert batching defaults permanently for now, ship hashing patch, add per-shard hard limiter, add an auto-eviction trigger when shard utilization > 70%.

oncall-lee: agree. I'll leave continuous batching paused until we validate rebalance and hashing patch in canary.

cs-omar: CS note: customers updated. they'll expect a postmortem and timeline for permanent fix. I'll collect affected request ids and attach logs to INC-4103.

eng-runtime-jess: quick debug snippet added to logs to help RCA: ```
# show per-shard mem and top prefixes
curl -s http://metrics/prod/kv/shards | jq '.shards[] | {id, mem_bytes, top_prefixes: .top[0:5]}'
```

sre-maya: capturing logs and archiving into incident bucket `s3://redwood-incidents/2330005678/` — saved current NCCL logs and eviction traces.

oncall-lee: handing off to day SRE oncall @sre-maya for follow-up/postmortem. I'll mark incident as mitigated but not resolved. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident 2330005678 status changed to MITIGATED by oncall-lee. Handoff to sre-maya.

sre-maya: acknowledged. I'll kick off full postmortem template and assign action items: hashing patch (eng-ml-aaron), limiter permanently enabled (infra-eli), batching config rollback monitoring (eng-runtime-jess), customer comms follow-through (cs-omar). Due EOD.

eng-ml-aaron: creating PR for hashing fix and adding tests to simulate prefix-hot keys. PR: `github.com/redwood/kv/compare/PR-4789`

eng-runtime-jess: will add auto-eviction rule to continuous batching controller.

cs-omar: will prepare customer-facing post-incident note and attach timeline.

pm-anna: also include follow-up: add a synthetic load that stresses shard distribution in pre-merge CI.

sre-maya: thanks all. final note: if anyone sees a reappearance ping here. I'll update the ticket and the postmortem doc when ready.

eng-ml-aaron: quick thumbs — :thumbsup:

oncall-lee: thanks team, great coordination.

incident-bot: This thread archived snapshot saved to incident timeline."
